title: fix(core): a bootstrap that fails after every plugin started rolls them back too
body:
Fixes #23644

Clause-②: no

`ObjectKernel.bootstrap()` rolled back started plugins only in the Phase 2 branch, for a plugin whose `start()` failed. A boot refused later (the system-requirement check, or a `kernel:ready`, `kernel:bootstrapped` or `kernel:listening` handler that throws) fell into the outer catch, which marks the kernel `stopped`, releases the signal listeners and rethrows. `shutdown()` on a stopped kernel is a no-op, so no plugin's `destroy()` ran and a driver connected in `start()` stayed connected. The live case is the dogfood refused boot in `organization-ownership-boot-refusal-order`, whose own docblock records the stale handle.

## What changed

`packages/core/src/kernel.ts`: the outer catch of `bootstrap()` now runs the same `rollbackStartedPlugins()` the Phase 2 branch runs, so a failed boot destroys the plugins that started, in reverse start order, at whatever phase it fails. Its existing duties are unchanged (state `stopped`, release the listeners, rethrow the original error). The catch's comment and the `rollbackOnFailure` TSDoc now state the new truth.

The rollback runs when `rollbackOnFailure && state === 'running' && startedPlugins.size > 0`:

- **`rollbackOnFailure`** is the Phase 2 branch's own gate, so `false` keeps opting out of both.
- **`startedPlugins.size > 0`** keeps a Phase 1 failure silent (nothing started) and makes the catch a no-op after the Phase 2 branch rolled back (`rollbackStartedPlugins()` clears the set), so a failing `start()` still rolls back exactly once.
- **`state === 'running'`, then `stopping` for the duration.** Two lines beyond the card's text, which I took so this change does not add a double destroy: a `shutdown()` that began mid-boot already owns the destroys (it destroys every plugin and the set is not cleared), and a `shutdown()` or signal arriving during the rollback is absorbed by the `stopping` state exactly as during a drain. Each has its own pin and its own ablation below; both come out cleanly if the seat prefers the minimal form.
- A `destroy()` that throws is handled by what the Phase 2 rollback already does: logged at `error` as `Rollback failed for NAME`, the loop continues, and the boot error is rethrown unchanged.

Not changed: the Phase 2 branch, `shutdown()`, `LiteKernel`, the lifecycle contract, the dogfood file, `packages/runtime`, `packages/verify`.

## Fork check (card: stop if the contract forbids it or `destroy()` is unsafe after `kernel:ready`)

- `packages/spec/src/contracts/plugin-lifecycle-events.ts` says nothing about a failed boot and does not forbid destroying plugins after one; `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx` already names `destroy()` "as rollback for plugins already started when a later plugin's start() fails" and the `bootPhaseHooks` TSDoc already says that a `destroy()` which assumes its boot-phase handler ran "must tolerate that it did not".
- Spot-read `destroy()` of the plugins that register a boot-phase hook: `HonoHttpServer.close()` returns when it never listened, `DefaultDatasourcePlugin.destroy` is best-effort around `disconnect`, `AuthPlugin.destroy` only nulls its manager, the job and queue services use optional chaining. No plugin found unsafe after a partial boot.

## Pins (`packages/core/src/kernel.failed-boot-rollback.test.ts`, 21 tests)

- **Tears down.**
  - A throw at `kernel:ready`, `kernel:bootstrapped`, `kernel:listening` and at the system-requirement check each destroys the started plugins in reverse start order and disconnects the fake driver connected in `start()` (exact sequence, so a double destroy reads red).
  - A `destroy()` that throws during the rollback neither replaces the boot error (identity) nor stops the plugin started before it.
  - The rollback runs with the kernel `stopping`, and a `shutdown()` called from inside a `destroy()` is absorbed.
- **Still one contract.**
  - CONTROL: the Phase 2 rollback (a `start()` that throws) destroys each started plugin once, in reverse order, and never the plugin whose `start()` threw.
  - `shutdown()` after a failure at each of the four sites destroys nothing more.
  - The rejection at each hook site is the original error object, and the readiness check rejects with its own.
  - `rollbackOnFailure: false` leaves the plugins and the driver untouched at each site.
  - A `shutdown()` that began mid-boot owns the destroys: the failed boot adds none.
  - A Phase 1 failure destroys nothing.

## Ablation (committed fix first; each mutation through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which proves the anchor hit, the blob change and the restore by blob equal to `HEAD` and an empty `git diff HEAD`)

The test imports `./kernel` by relative path, so there is no `dist/` leg to rebuild.

| Mutation (one at a time) | Red | Green |
|:---|:---|:---|
| delete the new `await this.rollbackStartedPlugins()` | 6: the four per-site tear-down pins, the throwing-`destroy()` pin, the `stopping` pin | 15: the control, `shutdown()` after failure x4, original rejection x4, `rollbackOnFailure: false` x4, mid-boot `shutdown()`, Phase 1 |
| remove `state === 'running'` | 1: mid-boot `shutdown()` owns the destroys | 20 |
| remove the `rollbackOnFailure` gate | 4: `rollbackOnFailure: false` x4 | 17 |
| remove `this.state = 'stopping'` | 1: the `stopping` pin | 20 |
| remove `this.startedPlugins.clear()` from `rollbackStartedPlugins` | 1: the Phase 2 control (a second rollback would double destroy) | 20 |

The observed direction is the usual one (red). Direction is not a template here: the first row's 15 greens are by design, each pins what a failed boot must NOT do and holds with or without the new call.

## Verification (head b2a5be7230d471d9d0d025aab7c698dbbc8e055a, `origin/main` merged at 286eb9ef32)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core typecheck`: exit 0 (`tsc`, the examples project, `check:test-typecheck` OK with the 4 pinned legacy errors unchanged).
- `@objectstack/core` tests: `local` project 101 files / 2494 tests passed; `repo` project 6 files / 83 tests passed.
- eslint (`--no-inline-config`) on the two changed source files: 0 errors, 0 warnings; 2 files read from `--format json`; type-aware linting is not enabled (`parserOptions` carries no `project`), so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.
- Gates from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` (63), the artifact-roster block (53) and the wide-population block (11), run after a full `turbo run build`: 123 of 127 exit 0. The four that exit non-zero need a PR number, a PR body or a workflow event payload (`check-closing-target-claim`, `check-partof-closing-keyword`, `check-single-claim-paths`, `pm/check-governed-queue-guard`): NOT MEASURED locally, their self-tests exit 0. Two gates exited 3 (prerequisite: no `dist/`) on the first pass and exit 0 after the build.
- The live case, read-only: `organization-ownership-boot-refusal-order.dogfood.test.ts` run against the rebuilt core: 4 of 4 passed, and its refused boot now logs `Bootstrap failed after plugins started — rolling back started plugins...` once and no `Rollback failed for`.

## Acceptance notes

- **Docs understate, still true.** `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx` (the `destroy()` comment and the `rollbackOnFailure: true` bullet) describes only the failing-`start()` rollback. Outside this card's file surface; not edited.
- **No timeout on the rollback.** `rollbackStartedPlugins()` awaits each `destroy()` with no deadline (`shutdown()` has `shutdownTimeout`), so a `destroy()` that never settles holds `bootstrap()` open. That was already true for the Phase 2 rollback and is now true for a late failure too. Not probed, not filed.
- **A plugin with no `start()` is never in `startedPlugins`,** so neither rollback destroys it (for example one that connects in `init()`). Existing contract of "started", unchanged.
- **`LiteKernel` has no rollback at all** (not on a failing `start()`, not on a late failure; its `destroy()` returns early once `stopped`). A different contract from the one this card extends; not read as a defect, not probed.
- **Idempotent teardown on the host side.** A host that closed the leaked resource by hand after a refused boot now closes it a second time; the changeset says so.
